The three notes files are clean. Each one keeps its original facts, and the checker reports no banned words and no long sentences.

## Headline

The procedure is in notes/procedure.md, and notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md now pass the checker.

- notes/a.md lost the banned word "clearly" and kept the speed claim.
- notes/b.md was one long sentence and is now three short sentences.
- notes/c.md lost the banned word "very" and is now four short sentences.

## Background

The request asked for a procedure file first. The procedure lists numbered steps that use the available tools to fix banned words and long sentences. The same steps then ran on notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md, in that order. Each file keeps its original meaning.

## Relevance

The checker is the acceptance test for these notes. A file that still holds a banned word or a sentence over 25 words fails that test.

## Information

The checker reports zero sentences over 25 words and no banned words for all three files. That result is a measurement from this session.

Assumption: a description sentence over 25 words is the only length rule that applies. Why not measured: the notes hold no instructions. Validate by: scan each file for an imperative. If wrong: split any instruction over 20 words.

Alternative considered: leave the long sentences and only drop banned words. That fails the length check, so it loses.

## End

I recommend that we do these actions.

1. Domain: Clear. The rule is known, so apply it. Increment: re-run the checker on the three notes. Blocker: an unseen edit can reintroduce a hit. Test first.

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences

Use this procedure on one notes file. The tools are list_files, read_file, write_file, and check_file.

1. Call read_file on the target path.
2. Mark each word from the banned list in Section 4.4 of the operating rules.
3. Count the words in each sentence. Flag a sentence over 25 words. Flag an instruction over 20 words.
4. Delete each banned word. Keep the same claim.
5. Split each flagged sentence into two or more sentences. Keep the same facts.
6. Call write_file with the full revised text. Do not change the title.
7. Call check_file on the same path.
8. If the check reports a hit, repeat steps 4 to 7. Stop when the check reports no hits.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service then fell back to the database for every request. That fallback lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. It writes the result to the store. It then marks the message as done so that no other worker picks it up again.
